name: Hydrocortisone
executiveSummary: Corticosteroid with mineralocorticoid activity. Adult adrenal crisis: **100 mg IV**, then **50 mg every 6 h** or **200 mg/day**. Septic shock: **200 mg/day** (50 mg q6h or infusion). Pediatric stress: **50–100 mg/m²/day** or **1–2 mg/kg every 6 h**.
indications:
## Indications

- Acute adrenal insufficiency / perioperative Addison coverage.
- Refractory septic shock (Surviving Sepsis — stress dose).
- Other: asthma/anaphylaxis as alternative corticosteroid in regimens.

## Precautions

- Hyperglycemia, Na+ retention/edema, hypertension, immunosuppression.
- Distinguish physiologic vs stress vs anti-inflammatory dosing.

> In adrenal crisis do not delay: give now and dose fluids/glucose.

adulto.dose: Adrenal crisis: **100 mg IV** immediately, then **50 mg every 6 h** (or **200 mg/day** continuous infusion). Septic shock: **200 mg/day** × ≥3 days if indicated. Anti-inflammatory/asthma: variable (**100–300 mg/day** divided).
adulto.administration: IV bolus 3–5 min or infusion; IM possible. Reconstitute with SW/NS/D5W.
adulto.notes: Switch to PO (e.g. 15–25 mg/day divided) when stable.

pediatrico.dose: Stress / adrenal: **50–100 mg/m²/day** divided every 6 h (or **1–2 mg/kg/dose** q6h). Crisis: bolus **50–100 mg/m²** then maintenance. Anti-inflammatory: **1–5 mg/kg/day**. Asthma attack: often **4–8 mg/kg** load then **2 mg/kg/dose** q6h.

neonatal.dose: Adrenal insufficiency: **1–2 mg/kg/dose** every 6–8 h (ranges **2–5 mg/kg** in crisis) — endocrinology/NNU.

adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Hyperglycemia, hypertension, edema, euphoria, immunosuppression, myopathy with prolonged use.
